source.title: The Neural Signatures of Shame, Embarrassment, and Guilt: A Voxel-Based Meta-Analysis on Functional Neuroimaging Studies

confidence_rationale: Quantitative voxel-based meta-analysis (17 guilt + 17 shame/embarrassment fMRI studies) showing partially DISSOCIABLE neural substrates whose functional interpretation maps onto the two REE branches: guilt -> left temporo-parietal junction (social cognition / other-modelling), shame/embarrassment -> dorsal ACC + thalamus (social-pain) and premotor cortex (behavioural inhibition / withdrawal). The behavioural-inhibition signature for shame and the social-cognitive signature for guilt are biological corroboration that the two are distinct action-tendency systems, grounding the ARC-097/INV-081 design split at the neural level. Held at 0.7 because functional labels of activation foci are interpretive, the harm-attribution-to-self that REE targets is not directly isolated, and species/substrate transfer to a synthetic agent is large.
failure_signatures: Guilt and shame/embarrassment share a common left anterior insula activation (emotional awareness/arousal) -- the dissociation is partial, not total, so a synthetic split that treats the two as cleanly separate streams overstates the neural evidence.

The meta-analysis pools shame with embarrassment, which differ in moral weight; the 'shame' signature is therefore not a pure index of moral self-condemnation, weakening the direct mapping to INV-081's specific target (global negative self-worth write).

mapping.source_claim_statement: Across 34 functional neuroimaging studies, guilt and shame/embarrassment both engage the left anterior insula (emotional awareness/arousal) but have dissociable specific substrates: guilt is associated with the left temporo-parietal junction (social-cognitive / mentalising processes), whereas shame/embarrassment recruit social-pain regions (dorsal anterior cingulate cortex, thalamus) and a behavioural-inhibition/premotor network. The authors interpret this as reflecting the distinct action tendencies of the two emotions.
mapping.ree_translation: Biological corroboration of the ARC-097 / INV-081 design split: the guilt branch carries a social-cognitive (other-directed, repair-relevant) signature, while the shame branch carries a social-pain + behavioural-inhibition (withdrawal) signature. This supports treating guilt-as-repair and shame-as-withdrawal as genuinely distinct routing targets -- the premise of routing self-attributed harm to repair (other-modelling) rather than to a withdrawing self-condemnation response.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The meta-analysis localises brain activation foci and assigns them functional labels by reverse inference; it does not measure the self-attribution-to-action computation REE prescribes, and it pools shame with embarrassment (which is less morally loaded), so the 'shame' signature is not a clean index of the global-self-badness write INV-081 prohibits. Transfer from human haemodynamic activation maps to a synthetic E3/self-model architecture is by analogy of function, not mechanism.
mapping.source_context: Voxel-based (ALE-style) meta-analysis of healthy-adult task-fMRI studies of self-conscious emotions; 17 shame/embarrassment and 17 guilt studies meeting inclusion criteria.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality good (quantitative meta-analysis aggregating 34 studies, peer-reviewed). Mapping fidelity moderate: the dissociable signatures corroborate the two-branch design but localisation/reverse-inference and the shame+embarrassment pooling dilute the specific mapping to INV-081. Transfer risk moderate-high: human fMRI to synthetic architecture.
